target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 120 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 22 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.abort-skip.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 198 passed
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary or a live Discord bot token, so a redacted live Discord conflict-to-success trace cannot be generated locally. Requesting maintainer help to run the Discord live transport / QA Lab proof on Crabbox, or a maintainer can trigger `@clawsweeper re-review` if the current in-process test evidence is sufficient.

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.shared-core.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |shared-core| src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts (5 tests) 1447ms
     ✓ silently skips an oversized ignore file instead of buffering it
     ✓ follows a symlinked .gitignore to a regular file
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.85s
```

- A 2.4 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file is silently skipped instead of buffering the whole file.
- A symlinked `.gitignore` is resolved and its regular target is still honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script that imports `addIgnoreRules` from `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` and exercises normal, large-but-under-cap, oversized, single-symlink, and chained-symlink `.gitignore` files in temp workspaces:

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js:      true
  ignores src/main.ts:      false

=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.4 MB) ===
  file size:              2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   true

=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB) ===
  file size:              13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   false

=== Single-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== Chained-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

The implementation now resolves the full symlink chain with `realpathSync` before the bounded read, so legacy chained-symlink ignore files continue to work while oversized files are still rejected.
